s1.syndrome_frame: Gastrointestinal symptoms in a patient with autoimmune disorders
salient_findings: Red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the gastric angle
Foveolar hyperplasia and mild degeneration of parietal cells
Mild lymphocytic infiltration and disorganized layer contours
key_facts: Patient has systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
Scheduled for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy before starting prednisolone
Never received acid-secretion inhibitors
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Endoscopy showed normal antrum and gastric corpus with red streaks on the lesser curvature
Magnified narrow-band imaging showed regular round pit patterns
Biopsy sites included greater curvature of the prepyloric area and lesser and greater curvatures of the gastric corpus
Histologic findings showed foveolar hyperplasia, mild degeneration of parietal cells, and mild lymphocytic infiltration
H+/K+-ATPase staining was heterogeneously reduced
Pepsinogen I staining was uneven
MUC6 staining was positive throughout the region
Chromogranin A staining showed slight enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia
Anti-parietal cell antibody was negative
Anti-intrinsic factor antibody was negative
Serum gastrin was within normal range
Vitamin B12 was within normal range
Anti-H. pylori IgG was negative

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has systemic lupus erythematosus and gastritis symptoms

shortlist.label: Chronic atrophic gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic findings show mild degeneration of parietal cells and mild lymphocytic infiltration

shortlist.label: Atrophic corpus gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic findings show foveolar hyperplasia and mild degeneration of parietal cells in the corpus region

raw.rationale: The patient's histologic findings, including foveolar hyperplasia, mild degeneration of parietal cells, and mild lymphocytic infiltration, along with heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining and uneven pepsinogen I staining, are consistent with chronic atrophic gastritis. The absence of anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibodies, as well as normal serum gastrin and vitamin B12 levels, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Autoimmune gastritis
rejected.why: Negative anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibodies

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome-associated gastritis
rejected.why: Lack of specific histologic findings characteristic of Sjögren's syndrome

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated gastritis
rejected.why: No specific histologic findings characteristic of systemic lupus erythematosus

rejected.label: Atrophic corpus gastritis
rejected.why: While some findings are consistent, chronic atrophic gastritis is a more comprehensive diagnosis that encompasses the patient's condition
